subject: Architecture
title: Angkor Wat: The Largest Religious Monument
description: A micro-lesson that makes Angkor Wat: The Largest Religious Monument usable.

hook.text: Angkor Wat covers 400 acres — larger than Vatican City — and was built as a single project.

buildup.text: King Suryavarman II built it as a Hindu temple in the 1100s. It later became Buddhist.

discovery.text: The temple faces west, breaking tradition. Scholars believe it was designed as a funerary monument.

twist.text: The jungle swallowed Angkor Wat for centuries. French explorers 'rediscovered' it in the 1860s.

climax.text: Its five towers symbolize Mount Meru, the mythical home of the gods in Hindu cosmology.

punchline.text: A city of gods, lost to the jungle, found by accident.

quiz.question: Why is Angkor Wat unusual among Khmer temples?
options: It was built using metal instead of stone
It faces west instead of the traditional east

details.summary: Angkor Wat in Cambodia is the world's largest religious monument, covering 162 hectares with a moat 190 meters wide. Built in the early 12th century as a Hindu temple dedicated to Vishnu, it was gradually converted to Buddhism.
details.whyItMatters: Angkor Wat demonstrates that medieval Southeast Asian civilization achieved architectural ambitions rivaling anything in Europe. Its scale, precision, and artistic program represent one of humanity's greatest cultural achievements.
takeaways: World's largest religious monument covering 162 hectares
Five towers represent Mount Meru from Hindu cosmology
Built in the 12th century, converted from Hindu to Buddhist use

faq.question: Why does Angkor Wat face west instead of east?
faq.answer: Most Khmer temples face east, but Angkor Wat faces west — the direction associated with Vishnu and also with death. Some scholars believe it functioned as a funerary temple for King Suryavarman II. The western orientation creates spectacular sunrise silhouettes from the front approach.

faq.question: How was Angkor Wat built?
faq.answer: An estimated 300,000 workers and 6,000 elephants moved over 5 million tons of sandstone from quarries 50 kilometers away. Blocks were transported by canal and raft, then precisely fitted without mortar. The entire complex was built in approximately 37 years.
